questions.question: In a Cartesian coordinate system in a plane, how is each point specified?
options: By a unique pair of real numbers.
By a single natural number.
By an unordered list of axes.
By the equation of a curve only.
questions.explanation: Two perpendicular oriented axes assign each plane point one ordered pair $(x,y)$ of real coordinates.
questions.source_support: Definition: each point in the plane is specified uniquely by a pair of real numbers.
option_explanations: One natural number cannot record independent displacement along two axes.
Axes are ordered and fixed; an unordered list does not locate a point.
A curve equation describes many possible points, not one unique point by itself.
questions.rewrite_notes: Hand-authored explanation + per-option explanations (why each wrong option is wrong + the likely misread).
